page.layout: One page of running text, with a heading at the top. Arabic and Hebrew words are set inline. No margin notes. A catchword at the foot right.

main_text.head: SECT. II. De literarum pronuntiatione, &c.
main_text.p: Literæ [illegible, ~8 letters] in dictionibus verè Persicis raro inveniuntur, adeò ut ubi ufurpantur, dictiones Arabicæ ferè omnes habendæ sunt, ut monet Lud. de Dieu.

[illegible, ~3 letters] facilè Persis cōfunduntur, ut & [illegible, ~2 letters] & [illegible, ~2 letters]. In Libris MSS. magnam difficultatem parit tum punctorum Diacriticorum tum vocalium abfentia, quum multæ dictiones punctis folùm & vocalibus diftinguuntur.
Primà dictionis vocalis, sequente immediate vocali alterâ, vix pronuntiatur, & idem ferè valet quod fcheva mobile apud Hebræ. ut [illegible, ~5 letters] criften flere.
In [illegible, ~2 letters] & [illegible, ~1 letter] sæpe duo ex tribus punctis omittuntur, præcipuè si [illegible, ~1 letter] immediatè sequatur, & tunc 5 puncta in tria coalescunt, ut fe-

page.notes: The first line has Arabic letters I cannot read reliably; the Arabic and Hebrew words are marked illegible with approximate letter counts. The printed line "fe-" and "quatur" is one word, so I kept the printed hyphen at the line end. The "ut" at the foot right is treated as a catchword, not text. The "ut" after the Hebrew word is the printed Latin conjunction. Show-through and the faint dots are not transcribed.
